quickAnswer: **Ahrefs Web Analytics** fits teams that want a **free, cookieless GA4 alternative** with SEO context in the Ahrefs ecosystem. Skip it if you need product analytics or tools outside Ahrefs — **Plausible**, **PostHog**, or **GA4** are stronger there.
bestFor: Marketing and SEO teams already using **Ahrefs** who want simple traffic reporting in the same dashboard
Site owners migrating off GA4 for a **privacy-friendly, cookie-free** script (~2 KB)
Teams tracking **AI referral traffic** (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, etc.) alongside classic referrers
Publishers who want **Google Search Console** keyword data next to on-site conversion funnels
notFor: Teams that do not want an Ahrefs account or SEO suite bundled with analytics
Product-led SaaS needing cohorts, feature flags, or session replay — use **PostHog** or **Hotjar**
Stripe-native revenue attribution — use **DataFast** or custom GA4 ecommerce
Self-hosted or open-source requirements — use **Umami** or **Plausible** self-hosted

sections.title: Privacy & compliance
sections.content:
Ahrefs Web Analytics is marketed as **cookie-free** and **privacy-friendly**, with **no personal data collected** in default configurations. That positions it alongside Plausible and Fathom for teams reducing consent-banner friction in the EU and UK — still verify with counsel for your tracking setup.

Because data lives in Ahrefs' cloud (Singapore-based company), data residency and DPA terms follow Ahrefs' platform policies, not your own infrastructure. This is a different tradeoff than self-hosted Umami or Matomo.

The lightweight script (~2 KB claimed) also reduces performance impact versus heavier GA4 tags.

Compare with [Plausible](/tools/plausible/), [Fathom](/tools/fathom/) and [Google Analytics 4](/tools/google-analytics-4/).

sections.title: Web analytics scope
sections.content:
Ahrefs covers core **marketing site metrics**: pageviews, referrers, devices, geography, **custom events**, **funnels**, and **outbound link** clicks. Real-time reporting is emphasized — visitors can appear within about a minute of an event.

Differentiators versus generic privacy analytics: **AI traffic breakdown** (which AI tools send visitors), **Search Console integration** for keyword-to-landing-page context, and **UTM** breakdowns for paid and partner campaigns.

Scope stays web/marketing focused — not a full product analytics or data warehouse platform. Historical data is described as **unlimited** on the product page, unlike GA4's retention limits.

sections.title: SEO & ecosystem integrations
sections.content:
Web Analytics is **included with Ahrefs Free** and sits inside the broader Ahrefs workspace alongside Site Explorer, Site Audit, and Rank Tracker on paid plans. That integration is the main reason to choose it over standalone Plausible — your traffic data lives next to SEO workflows.

**Google Search Console** connection is a headline feature for tying rankings to on-site behavior. There is no native Google Ads or BigQuery export comparable to GA4's marketing platform depth.

You can **import historical data from GA4** to ease migration, which lowers switching friction for teams leaving Google Analytics.

sections.title: Cloud-only deployment
sections.content:
Ahrefs Web Analytics is **cloud-only SaaS** — install a JavaScript snippet or use GA4 import, then manage projects in the Ahrefs dashboard. Verified domain ownership is required for the free tier.

There is no self-hosted edition. Teams with strict data-sovereignty requirements should compare **Matomo** or **Umami** instead.

Setup is intentionally simple (copy-paste snippet, installation checker) and aimed at marketers rather than data engineers.

setupNotes:
**Typical setup:**

1. Create or sign in to an **Ahrefs Free** account.
2. Add a **Web Analytics** project and verify site ownership.
3. Paste the **JavaScript snippet** into your site `<head>` (or use the GA4 import path if migrating).
4. Run the in-app **installation check** to confirm events are flowing.
5. Optionally connect **Google Search Console** and configure **custom events** or **funnels** for key conversions.

No tag manager is required, though you can deploy via GTM if preferred.

**Common pitfalls:** mixing Ahrefs event counts with GA4 pageview definitions, forgetting verification for the free tier, and tracking staging domains you did not intend to bill against project limits.
pricingNotes:
Ahrefs documents the free Web Analytics limit as **1 million page views** in one place and **1 million events** in another, per verified project per month on Ahrefs Free. Above that, **per-project add-ons** scale limits — Ahrefs documents tiers at roughly **$99/month (up to 5M events)**, **$299/month (20M)**, and **$999/month (100M)** per project as of Sep 2026.

This is separate from Ahrefs SEO subscriptions (Lite, Standard, Advanced), though Web Analytics appears across plans. High-traffic sites pay per project for headroom, not a single global pool.

Use our [pricing calculator](/calculators/pricing/) to estimate Web Analytics add-on cost at your event volume.
limitations: Requires an Ahrefs account — not a standalone analytics SKU you can buy in isolation from the platform.
No session replay, heatmaps, or product analytics depth — pair with Hotjar or PostHog if needed.
Cloud-only — no self-hosted or open-source path.
No public affiliate program — AnalyticsVS links direct to Ahrefs (no commission).
Script performance benchmark pending on AnalyticsVS.

faq.question: Is Ahrefs Web Analytics free?
faq.answer: Yes, Ahrefs Web Analytics is free for websites with verified ownership, up to 1 million events per month per project, and a free Ahrefs account can add as many sites as you want. Higher volumes need a paid per-project add-on (see pricing below).

faq.question: Does Ahrefs Web Analytics use cookies, and is it GDPR compliant?
faq.answer: It uses no cookies and stores no IP addresses with analytics data. Unique visitors are counted with a hash of IP address and user agent plus a salt that is regenerated every 24 hours, so visitors cannot be tracked across days, devices or other sites. Ahrefs states that site owners remain responsible for their own GDPR obligations, so check your setup with counsel.

faq.question: Ahrefs Web Analytics vs Google Analytics 4: what is the difference?
faq.answer: Ahrefs is a lighter, cookie-free alternative focused on traffic, SEO and AI referrals, while GA4 is a full marketing analytics platform. Ahrefs' own comparison lists zero cookies vs GA4's first-party cookies, data available instantly vs 24-48 hours, a 2 KB script vs about 98 KB, and unlimited historical data vs 26 months. GA4 remains stronger for Google Ads, audiences and BigQuery export, and Ahrefs can import GA4 data if you switch.

faq.question: How much does Ahrefs Web Analytics cost above the free limit?
faq.answer: Above 1 million events a month, Ahrefs charges per project: up to 5M events for $99/month, up to 20M for $299/month and up to 100M for $999/month (USD; Ahrefs notes prices can vary by location). Features on every tier include AI traffic reports (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini), Search Console keywords, funnels, custom events, UTM breakdowns and outbound link tracking.

faq.question: Ahrefs vs Plausible or Fathom?
faq.answer: Plausible and Fathom are standalone privacy analytics tools with simpler vendor relationships. Ahrefs fits when you already use or plan to use Ahrefs for SEO and want analytics beside that workflow — especially AI traffic and Search Console context.

faq.question: Can I migrate from GA4?
faq.answer: Ahrefs offers GA4 data import to bring historical context into Web Analytics. You will still want to run both in parallel briefly to validate metric differences before switching reporting.
